# Component structure & composition — knowledge base

Extracted from the SFCC-55 footer session (18–21 Aug 2026), verified against the live repo
at `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui` and `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app@10.0.0`.

Scope: folder structure/naming, the atomic model, `ccExtensibility` override mechanics, the SFCC
bridge pattern, container/presentational separation, component API design, the component
registry, and dev catalogues vs Storybook.

**Every claim below marked VERIFIED was executed against the working tree, not read from the
transcript.** Where the session contradicted itself, the *latest* position is given and the
retraction is called out — the retraction is usually the real lesson.

---

## (a) RULES

### A1. Placement is decided: `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/index.tsx`

New Zimmermann-authored design-system components go at:

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/<tier>/<camelCase>/index.tsx
                                        index.stories.tsx
```

**VERIFIED live on this branch** (`ls overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`):

| Tier | Present |
|---|---|
| `atoms/` | `zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput` (5) |
| `molecules/` | `zimmInputAction` (1) |
| `organisms/` | **directory does not exist** — no organism has been placed here yet |

This matches the agreed state exactly. Note `organisms/` is *absent*, not empty — the first
organism placed there creates it.

**Do not read the earlier "build flat, don't create `atoms/`" analysis as current.** That was
the 2026-08-19T03:32:59 position and it was superseded later in the same session. Git history
confirms the reversal in order:

- `dc86c13 refactor(ui-kit): migrate ZimmButton to Chakra Button+button.ts…` — moved
  `overrides/app/ui-kits/` → `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`, converted flat files
  (`zimmButton.tsx`) to folder-per-component (`zimmButton/index.tsx`), and **flattened the tiers**.
- `39ad495 refactor(ui-kits): organise components into atoms/ and molecules/ subdirectories` —
  pure `R100`/`R094` renames, 0 line changes, **tiers restored**.

Why the move under `components/` mattered: `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` scans
`overrides/app/components/`. At the old top-level `overrides/app/ui-kits/` path these components
were invisible to the registry. **Anything placed outside `overrides/app/components/` is
registry-invisible.**

### A2. Casing is three families. Each is correct in its own; never generalise between them

| Family | Casing | Example | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | kebab-case | `components/footer/`, `components/product-tile/` | **Must** byte-match upstream's path or the resolver never fires |
| ui-kit component | camelCase | `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/` | `conventions.md` default for Zimmermann-authored files |
| `shared/ui` primitive | PascalCase | `components/shared/ui/Button/` | Mirrors upstream's own PascalCase |

A fourth, separate rule: **the theme recipe key is PascalCase while the recipe file is
camelCase.** VERIFIED in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`: files `zimmTextInput.ts`,
`zimmNavItem.ts`, `footer.ts` export keys `ZimmTextInput`, `ZimmNavItem`, `ZimmFooter`.

### A3. Tier is derived from what the component's OWN template renders — never from visual size

Verbatim from `f2r/.claude/skills/_shared/atomic-model.md` (**VERIFIED** present on branch
`f2r-component-registry`; **not** on `f2r-implementation-workflow`, which has the built
components but not the doc):

| Tier | Definition (by what the component's **own template renders**) |
|---|---|
| **Atom** | Renders **no other component**: markup + CSS + tokens only. `composes: []` |
| **Molecule** | Renders **only atoms** |
| **Organism** | Renders **at least one** molecule |
| **Template** | Skeletal page frame: named regions, arrangement, responsive. No real content. Renders ≥1 organism |
| **Page** | A template instance with real content applied |

The six named rules, which settle the arguments people actually have:

- **Rule A — icons are attributes, not components.** A glyph delivered by an attribute value
  (`icon="arrow-right"`) composes nothing. A Button with a leading icon is **still an atom**.
  Only a standalone displayed glyph is the `Icon` atom.
- **Rule B — slot ≠ import.** Slotted children do **not** change the parent's tier. Only what
  the parent's own template renders counts.
- **Rule C — Template defines structure, not content.** Real copy/imagery ⇒ it's a Page.
- **Rule D — a Page is always an instance of exactly one template.**
- **Rule E — layout sections are not components.** Blocks/sections are layout instructions
  (spacing, background, container-query sizing), not contract entries. Classify by structural
  role, not visual scale.
- **Rule F — templates and pages are not delivered.** *"The design system provides atoms,
  molecules, and organisms. How a developer assembles those into a page frame within their
  stack … is outside the scope of the component library."*

Three edge tests, applied in order: decorative internals (badge dot, toggle knob, slider thumb)
do not bump the tier; an atom-only region is a **molecule** even if it spans the full viewport;
containers follow their own template.

**Rule F is the handoff boundary.** F2R delivers atoms/molecules/organisms; page assembly is
ours. This is the cleanest statement of the F2R↔app contract in the project.

Tier is **derived, not declared**: the contract records `composes: [...]` per component and
`validate.mjs` computes the tier transitively, so it cannot drift. When porting from F2R, read
the tier off `composes` rather than judging it, and add `@see f2r/02-design/library/elements/<name>`
to the JSDoc.

Cross-check that the built components honour it: `ZimmInputAction` composes `ZimmTextInput` +
`ZimmButton` (two atoms) ⇒ **molecule** ✓. `Footer` renders `ZimmInputAction` (a molecule) ⇒
**organism** ✓.

### A4. An SFCC override outranks the ui-kit tier for placement

The footer is an **organism** by A3, yet it lives at `overrides/app/components/footer/`, not
`ui-kits/organisms/zimmFooter/`. That is correct, and it is a general rule: **if a component
must intercept an upstream SFCC import path, the kebab-cased mirror path wins over the ui-kits
tier path.** The tier is still true of the component; it just isn't expressed in the folder.

### A5. The styling surface is a theme recipe. Always

Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` global class, not co-located CSS. For a bespoke component
wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is the bridge and the recipe is read via
`useMultiStyleConfig` / `useStyleConfig`.

- **Single-part recipe → `useStyleConfig`.** VERIFIED: `zimmNavItem/index.tsx` does
  `useStyleConfig('ZimmNavItem', {variant})` → `__css={styles}`.
- **Multi-part recipe → `useMultiStyleConfig`.** VERIFIED: `zimmTextInput/index.tsx` does
  `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmTextInput', {...})` → `__css={styles.root}`, `styles.row`, …
  Same in `footer/index.tsx` (`useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmFooter')`, 69 `chakra.*` call sites).

The reason against co-located CSS is worth carrying because it is not obvious: **a stylesheet
can only see `var(--zimm-*)`, which is derived output at the bottom of the token pipeline.**
Authoring there forfeits `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens,
responsive arrays, and the theme drift-guard tests.

F2R's `.styles.ts` files (Emotion + `.zimm-*` classes) are good raw *material* — convert them
into a recipe; do not copy the pattern. Never reintroduce `.zimm-btn-*`.

### A6. Register the recipe in `theme/components/index.ts` or it throws at runtime

VERIFIED contents:

```ts
import { Button } from './button';
import { ZimmFooter } from './footer';
import { Header } from './header';
import { ListMenu } from './listMenu';
import { ZimmNavItem } from './zimmNavItem';
import { ZimmTextInput } from './zimmTextInput';
export const components = { Button, ZimmFooter, Header, ListMenu, ZimmNavItem, ZimmTextInput };
```

Note `zimmIcon` and `zimmLogo` have **no** recipe (they need none), and `zimmButton` reuses the
existing `Button` recipe rather than adding one. Adding a recipe is not automatic per component.

### A7. Namespace a recipe key that collides with a base SFCC component name

`extendTheme` **deep-merges**. A recipe named `Footer` would *inherit* base SFCC's `Footer`
rather than replace it. VERIFIED in `footer/index.tsx`:

```ts
/** Theme recipe key. Namespaced rather than 'Footer' because extendTheme deep-merges — a recipe
 *  named Footer would inherit base SFCC's Footer instead of replacing it. Must match the key
 *  registered in theme/components/index.ts; a typo here silently yields an empty style object. */
const ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE = 'ZimmFooter';
```

Two rules in one: **namespace colliding keys `Zimm*`**, and **a typo in the key silently yields
an empty style object** — no error, just an unstyled component. Bind the key to a named constant
so it is greppable and typo-visible.

### A8. Container/presentational — the container is the *default* export, the presentational
component is the *named* export

The ratified rule (`components.md`) is: anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data
as props and does not call data-fetching hooks. SFCC's base `_app` renders `<Footer />` with
**no props**, so for a shell component there is no upstream container to own the data. The
resolution used, VERIFIED in `footer/index.tsx`:

```tsx
export const Footer = ({ data, /* required, no default */ … }: FooterProps) => { … }   // presentational

const FooterContainer = (props: Omit<FooterProps, 'data'>) => {   // the seam
  const { buildUrl } = useMultiSite();
  const history = useHistory();
  return <Footer data={FOOTER_FIXTURE} onLogoClick={() => history.push(buildUrl(HOME_HREF))} {...props} />;
};
export default FooterContainer;
```

The pattern generalises: **presentational named export with required data + a thin default-export
container that is the only place static content or navigation wiring lives.** Stories and tests
import the named export and pass data explicitly; the app gets the default export.

### A9. Static fixtures live in the container or the story — never as a prop default

`data = FOOTER_FIXTURE` as a **default parameter** is the defect, not the fixture itself. It
moves placeholder content from the story into the runtime contract, so absent CMS data becomes
indistinguishable from present CMS data. Consequences observed: 18 `href="#"` dead links; AU-only
"Acknowledgement of Country" rendering on all 11 sites; and no pressure to schedule the CMS story
because the footer *looks* finished.

The final state removes the default (`data: FooterConfigEntry`, required — VERIFIED in the
registry row and the type) and supplies the fixture from `FooterContainer` instead.

Note the session's own zig-zag here, because the reasoning matters: "render nothing when data is
absent" was proposed, then **retracted** — it would have removed the footer from the per-branch
preview environment, which is the surface the designer reviews against Figma. Optimising for the
rule broke the workflow. The container split is what satisfies both.

### A10. Per-item absence guards survive the integration — write them now

Independently of when the CMS lands, **a business user can save a nav link with a label and a
blank href.** So guard per item, not just per payload:

```tsx
href ? <chakra.a href={href} aria-label={label}>…</chakra.a>
     : <chakra.span aria-hidden={true}>…</chakra.span>   // visible but inert; not keyboard-reachable
```

VERIFIED as the shipped `ZimmNavItem` behaviour, expressed as element choice rather than a
caller-side ternary: renders `<a>` when `href` is present *and* passes `isSafeHref`, otherwise a
`<button type="button">` with no navigation side-effect — "no fragment scroll, no redirect for
placeholder items."

### A11. Component API — discriminated union when variants have genuinely different contracts

VERIFIED `zimmButton/index.tsx`:

```ts
type ZimmButtonBaseProps = { label: string; type?: …; disabled?: boolean; inverse?: boolean; … };
type ZimmLabelButtonProps = ZimmButtonBaseProps & { variant?: 'primary'|'secondary'; size?: 'large'|'medium'; fullWidth?: boolean };
type ZimmIconButtonProps  = ZimmButtonBaseProps & { variant: 'icon'; icon: ZimmIconType; size?: ZimmIconSize };
type ZimmButtonProps = ZimmLabelButtonProps | ZimmIconButtonProps;
```

What the union buys, all of which a flat optional-props type would lose:
- `variant: 'icon'` **requires** `icon`; the label variants forbid it.
- `fullWidth` is unavailable on the icon variant.
- `size` legitimately means different things per member (`'large'|'medium'` vs `ZimmIconSize`).
- **The a11y contract is encoded in the type**: `label` is required in *both* members, and
  doubles as the visible text (label variants) or the `aria-label` (icon variant, which renders
  no visible text). It is impossible to construct an unlabelled icon button.

### A12. Opt-in, defaulting off, for any affordance not in the design-system spec

Do not let an atom impose an affordance the spec does not define; do not delete it either if it
is plausibly useful to another consumer. Make it opt-in and say why at the point of use.
VERIFIED `zimmTextInput/index.tsx` — `clearable?: boolean` defaulting `false`, with a JSDoc that
records the spec absence, the confirmation that resolved it, and the reason for keeping it:

> *"Kept as opt-in rather than deleted because a clear affordance is reasonable on a text input
> atom (a search field would want one) — it just should not be the atom's decision to impose.
> No consumer opts in today."*

The audit confirms `clearable` has **0 consumers** — which is the intended outcome, not a gap.

### A13. Slot props are the atom→molecule seam. Test them at the consumer

`trailing?: React.ReactNode` is an empty hole at the right-hand end of the input.
`ZimmTextInput` has no idea what goes in it; `ZimmInputAction` puts the submit chevron there.
That slot **is** the entire mechanism connecting the atom to the molecule.

Two rules follow:
1. **A slot prop tied to a spec attribute should say so.** VERIFIED JSDoc maps `trailing` to the
   extracted TextfieldV2 spec's `trailing-icon` attribute with a Figma node id. That is what
   distinguishes it from `clearable`, which has no spec backing.
2. **A slot prop's correct test level is the consumer that fills it** — see T7.

### A14. Prefer `sx` over `style` on a themed component, and say so in the prop docs

VERIFIED `ZimmNavItem` exposes both and documents the preference inline:
`/** Theme-resolved style overrides. Preferred over 'style' — token keys resolve. */`.
`style` is an inline style: highest specificity, unoverridable, token keys do **not** resolve.

### A15. Before scoping any story around "override X and it propagates", grep who imports X

```bash
grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

This one command is the difference between A15 working and Trap T1.

---

## (b) TRAPS

### T1. `shared/ui` — the override that intercepts nothing

- **Symptom.** You override `overrides/app/components/shared/ui/Button/`, expecting every base
  SFCC screen (cart, checkout, account) to inherit branded buttons for free. It compiles,
  resolves, and changes nothing anywhere.
- **Root cause (VERIFIED).** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui/index.jsx:29`
  is `export {Button} from './Button'` — a **relative** specifier. `ccExtensibility` only
  rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` specifiers; a relative import inside `node_modules`
  is never touched. And the consumption pattern is the wrong way round: **208 base files import
  the barrel; 0 import `shared/ui/Button`.** (Both counts re-verified by grep.) Upstream
  `shared/ui/Button/index.jsx` is literally `export {Button} from '@chakra-ui/react'`.
- **Fix.** Do not rely on it propagating. Either (Option A) create
  `overrides/app/components/shared/ui/index.tsx` re-exporting your versions — which *does*
  intercept, but then hits all 208 base files, i.e. you restyle SFCC whether you wanted to or
  not; or (Option B) import `shared/ui/<Name>` directly from your own code and leave the barrel
  alone. See O2.
- **Why it's worth remembering.** This was asserted confidently ("the highest-leverage component
  decision available in a slim-overrides project", "ratify it explicitly") and then **retracted
  in full**: *"I previously told you that overriding `shared/ui/` means 'the entire base template
  inherits your version — zero call sites touched.' That is not how it resolves."* The idea reads
  as obviously correct and the failure is invisible.
- **The general claim still holds for ordinary overrides.** `breadcrumb`, `product-tile`,
  `display-price` *are* imported by full package path, so those do intercept.

### T2. Overriding `footer` does not reach `/checkout`

- **Symptom.** The branded footer is on every page except checkout, which shows the Salesforce
  demo footer ("This is a demo store only. Orders made WILL NOT be processed.") on all 8
  storefronts.
- **Root cause (VERIFIED).** Base `_app/index.jsx:484` is
  `{!isCheckout ? <Footer /> : <CheckoutFooter />}`, and `CheckoutFooter` is imported from
  `app/pages/checkout/partials/checkout-footer` — a **different module** that your `footer`
  override does not shadow.
- **Fix.** Overriding a component only intercepts the paths that import *that* path. Where base
  code branches to a sibling component, you must override the sibling too (here:
  `pages/checkout/partials/checkout-footer`). Generalise: **grep for conditional renders of
  alternates, not just for imports of your own path.**

### T3. The resolver does not run in Storybook or Vitest

- **Symptom.** A story or unit test appears to exercise your override and silently renders the
  unstyled base SFCC component.
- **Root cause.** `ccExtensibility` (declared in `package.json` as
  `{"extends": "@salesforce/retail-react-app", "overridesDir": "overrides"}` — VERIFIED) is read
  by a webpack plugin and runs only in the real app build. `.storybook/main.js` aliases the
  package straight to `node_modules`; `vitest.config.ts` does not touch it.
- **Fix.** Inside an override, import an *already-overridden* component by **relative path**
  (`'../swatch-group'`), not by base path. Base-path imports are still correct for modules you
  are **not** also overriding. Already documented in `overrideStyling.md`; T1 is the same family.

### T4. An explicit re-export shadows `export *` in the icons barrel

- **Symptom.** You add an icon to `icons/zimm.tsx`, and the app keeps rendering Salesforce's
  glyph. No error.
- **Root cause (from the session, matches the icons barrel structure).** `icons/index.tsx`
  carries explicit named re-exports alongside `export *`; an explicit re-export wins, so adding
  to `zimm.tsx` alone is silently ignored.
- **Fix.** Edit **both** files. Then verify what actually rendered (the session checked
  `viewBox`, `stroke="currentColor"`, `usesSprite: false`) rather than assuming.

### T5. Chakra's own style props beat your recipe

- **Symptom.** `button.ts` sets `p: 'xs'` for the icon size; the rendered submit control measures
  16×16 with `padding: 0px`, failing WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (24×24). The theme value is **dead code**.
- **Root cause.** Chakra's `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"` as a **style prop**, and style
  props beat recipe values.
- **Fix.** When wrapping a Chakra component, verify the computed value in a browser rather than
  trusting the recipe. Where a Chakra component hard-sets the property you need, set it at the
  call site (or use `chakra.button` + your own recipe instead of the Chakra component).
- **Bonus instance of the same shape:** the 24px minimum *does* exist in
  `zimmTextInput.ts:153-156` citing SC 2.5.8 — but on the `clearButton` slot, which has no
  consumer. The `{trailing}` slot carrying the real submit has no styles. **A rule enforced on
  the wrong slot is not enforced.**

### T6. The registry's TS prop extractor cannot read a union alias — and fails *open*

- **Symptom.** `.claude/registry/components.md` advertised `ZimmButton` as having
  `label: string` **and** a required `icon: ZimmIconType` — a combination the type forbids.
- **Root cause.** `extractTsProps`' block regex requires an object-literal body, so a union alias
  (`type ZimmButtonProps = A | B`) never matched and fell through to a **merge-everything
  fallback**, flattening mutually-exclusive variants into one row.
- **Fix, in two commits, both worth reading (`13add6e`, then `ec9d161`).** The second is the
  instructive one, because the first fix introduced two new defects:
  1. **Partial unions were published as complete.** `.filter(Boolean)` dropped members declared
     in other files, and the bail-out only fired when *every* member failed. With
     `members.length` shrunk to 1, every surviving prop trivially satisfied the
     "present in every member" test and was reported **required**. Now all-or-nothing: if any
     member is unresolvable, the union expression is returned verbatim.
  2. **Requiredness depended on declaration order.** Reversing `ZimmButton`'s operands turned
     `variant?: 'primary'|'secondary'` into `variant: 'icon'`. A prop is now required only where
     **every** member carries it **and every member declares it without `?`**; types are unioned
     across members instead of taken from whichever operand came first. Within a member, an
     intersection may declare a prop twice, so the member requires it if **any** declaration does.
- **Transferable lesson.** *"A regex standing in for real parsing"* — and the same class of error
  recurred later in a story-coverage audit (T7). A tool that reports a *proxy* as a *finding*
  will fail open: it produced a confident, wrong, machine-generated claim that a discriminated
  union does not hold.

### T7. Counting prop references in a component's own story file cannot detect slot coverage

- **Symptom.** An audit reported `ZimmTextInput.trailing` as "zero story coverage, one production
  usage" and concluded `ZimmTextInput` was "the one genuinely incomplete atom in the footer build."
- **Root cause.** The audit counted, per declared prop, references in *that component's* story
  file. That single metric cannot distinguish (i) a prop with no coverage anywhere, (ii) a prop
  covered by its consumer, and (iii) a prop nothing uses at all. **All three return `0`.**
- **Fix / retraction.** `trailing` is a **slot prop** — being exercised through the consumer that
  fills it is the *correct* level, not a lesser substitute. Three
  `getByRole('button', {name: /submit/i})` calls in `ZimmInputAction`'s plays would throw
  immediately if it broke. Corrected verdict: *"no untested load-bearing behaviour"*; the real
  residue is four **declared-but-unused** props (`value`, `defaultValue`, `ZimmIcon.color`,
  `ZimmNavItem.onClick`) where the question is whether to **trim the API**, not whether to write
  stories.
- **Rule.** Resolve every `0` before reporting it. For a slot prop, look at the consumer.

### T8. `overrideStyling.md` is ratified but its examples do not exist on this branch

- **Symptom.** A developer follows the rules file and hits dead ends.
- **VERIFIED** — of 11 paths the file cites, **10 are missing** on this branch:
  `overrides/app/components/product-tile/index.tsx`, `swatch-group`, `link/index.tsx`,
  `display-price`, `image-gallery`, `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`, `.claude/rules/overrides.md`,
  `theme/components/imageGallery.ts`, `swatchGroup.ts`, `link.ts`. Only
  `theme/components/button.ts` exists.
- **Consequences specific to this domain.** (i) The **SFCC bridge pattern** has *no live example*
  in the repo — its stated precedent (`product-tile`'s `CardBaseline` + default) is on another
  branch, so nobody can copy it. (ii) The file **mandates** running
  `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` before any PR touching `overrides/app/components/**` — the
  enforcement mechanism for the whole styling standard **does not exist**. (iii)
  `.claude/rules/overrides.md`, cross-referenced three times, is absent.
- **Fix.** Treat `overrideStyling.md`'s *rules* as binding and its *file citations* as aspirational
  until the referenced components land. Do not conclude a rule is void because its example is missing.

### T9. The registry's tier table is a hand-copied second source of truth

- **VERIFIED** `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs:122` — `// Tier + squad classification — mirrors .claude/rules/`
  followed by hardcoded `TIER1_PATHS` / `TIER2_PATHS` / `SQUAD_A_PATHS` / `SQUAD_B_PATHS` arrays.
  "Mirrors" means "duplicates", so it can drift from `frozenFiles.md` / `protectedFiles.md`.
- **Concrete drift already present.** `TIER1_PATHS` omits `app/theme/index.ts`,
  `overrides/app/config/countries.ts`, `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`, `babel.config.js`,
  `tsconfig.json`, `.github/workflows/`, `mobify.config.js` — all Tier 1 per `frozenFiles.md`.
- **The trap that bites this domain.** `getTier()` returns `'4 — Feature-local'` for anything
  unmatched, and **no `ui-kits` path is listed**. So every design-system atom — the components
  with the widest blast radius in the app — is reported as **Tier 4 Feature-local**. VERIFIED in
  `.claude/registry/components.md`: `ZimmButton`, `ZimmIcon`, `ZimmLogo`, `ZimmNavItem`,
  `ZimmTextInput`, `ZimmInputAction` all show `4 — Feature-local`.
- Also note there is no Tier 3: the scale is 1, 2, 4.
- **Fix.** Do not use the registry's Tier column as authority. `frozenFiles.md` /
  `protectedFiles.md` are the source; the registry is a convenience index.

### T10. Four Zimmermann buttons still exist across branches; one is dead in-tree

At the time of the analysis: `components/button/` (develop), `components/shared/ui/Button/`
(`pdp-token-class-spike`), `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton.tsx` (PR #55, flat), and
`components/ui-kits/atoms/zimm-button/` (Han's F2R, kebab + Emotion).

**VERIFIED on this branch:** `overrides/app/components/button/` still exists and has **zero
consumers** — the only greps that hit it are JSDoc/comment references to `theme/components/button.ts`,
not imports. It is pre-existing dead code, not something this work introduced. `ZimmButton` is
the live one and it reuses the same `Button` recipe.

### T11. F2R's `zimm-button.styles.ts` re-creates the exact seven classes PR #56 deleted

Name-by-name: `.zimm-btn`, `.zimm-btn-full`, `.zimm-btn-icon`, `.zimm-btn-large`,
`.zimm-btn-medium`, `.zimm-btn-primary`, `.zimm-btn-secondary` — with near-identical CSS.

Worth getting the reasoning right before arguing it: #56's *stated* objection was that a static
class *"can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible`"*. **That stated reason is
wrong** — plain CSS expresses `:hover`/`:active`/`:disabled`/`:focus-visible` perfectly well, and
F2R's does. #56's *real* objection was to a class **mirroring** a Chakra recipe: two sources of
truth for one component. F2R's isn't a mirror — its components aren't Chakra components, so the
class *is* its single source.

So the genuine fork is not "class vs recipe" but: **#56 assumes Chakra-component delivery; F2R
delivers framework-agnostic React + CSS.** Both are internally coherent; both cannot own the
button. Per A5 the decision went to the recipe, and F2R `.styles.ts` files are raw material to
convert — but the *reason* recorded in A5 (the `var(--zimm-*)`-only visibility of a stylesheet) is
the durable one, not the "can't express states" claim.

### T12. Inline styles + React state for interaction (mechanism "E") — rejected, and why

The original `ZimmButton` hand-rolled `useState(hovered/pressed/focused)` with inline styles.
Costs, all of which apply to any component tempted down this road:
- Interaction states are **dead until hydration** — bad against a ≤2s p75 mobile LCP budget.
- No `@media (hover: hover)`, so touch devices get sticky hover after tap.
- The recipe's `_focusVisible` focus ring (WCAG 2.4.7) does not apply — the component
  reimplements focus and inherits none of the a11y work.
- Inline styles are **unoverridable**: a designer token change routed through the theme literally
  cannot reach the component, and neither can a future Chakra variant.
- Every hover re-renders the component.

`dc86c13` migrated it to Chakra `Button` + `button.ts`. Do not reintroduce it.

### T13. Sub-components inside a parent file sit outside ui-kit governance

`footer/index.tsx` contains four internal sub-components (`SubscribeModal`, `SubscribeSection`,
`ContactIconRow`, `BottomBar`). `components.md` explicitly permits internal sub-components without
their own stories, so this is **conformant** — but they are invisible to the registry, carry no
tier, and are covered only via the parent's stories. Fine for genuinely single-parent pieces; a
signal to promote to the ui-kit the moment a second consumer appears.

### O1. Reconciling F2R's kebab-cased folders with the agreed camelCase

- **Situation.** Branch `f2r-implementation-workflow` (**VERIFIED**) has a fully-built hierarchy

  there is now a live precedent in-tree, and two casings for one family is exactly the ambiguity
  the decision closed.
- **Option B — keep kebab as a stated exception.** The folder name would equal the custom-element
  name would equal the contract entry, giving mechanical traceability back to `composes: [...]`.
  Strongest argument: the tier is *derived* from the contract, so the contract link is
  load-bearing, not cosmetic — and an exception that is written down is not ambiguity.
- Whichever way: `@see f2r/02-design/library/elements/<name>` in the JSDoc preserves the
  traceability even under Option A, which weakens B considerably.
- **Merge cost to price in:** Han's branches **predate PR #56** and carry their own full
  `theme/foundation/` (colour, typography, spacing, sizes, zimmTokens, globalStyles), so the merge
  conflicts substantially with #56's derived-foundation model. Note also `.claude/ui-kits/BUILD-LOG.md`
  and `DESIGNER-REVIEW.md` on that branch — a parallel governance surface.

### O2. The `shared/ui` barrel: Option A or Option B (genuinely unresolved)

Given T1, there are exactly two coherent choices:
- **Option A — create `overrides/app/components/shared/ui/index.tsx`** re-exporting Zimmermann
  versions and passing the rest through. All Contentful components get branded primitives with
  zero import changes. **Strongest argument:** least work, and it is the only thing that actually
  intercepts. **Cost:** it also hits the 208 base files, so you restyle SFCC after all — the
  opposite of the stated "we won't use the SFCC overridden components" intent. You have to *want*
  that.
- **Option B — import `shared/ui/<Name>` directly** from our own code, leave the barrel alone.
  **Strongest argument:** matches the stated purpose exactly — a CMS rich-text renderer mapping a
  `hyperlink` node to a `Link` wants something predictable and unopinionated, not a component
  carrying SFCC's locale-routing and commerce behaviour. **Cost:** you touch each import site, and
  nothing stops someone reaching for the barrel out of habit.
- **Context that makes this real, not theoretical (VERIFIED on `develop`).** Every Contentful
  component already pulls primitives from the barrel: `duplexSection` (Box, Text),
  `collectionHero` (Box, Button, Heading, Text), `hotspotPopup` (Box, Image, Link, Skeleton,
  Text), `imageText`, `heroBanner`, `shoppableImage`. So `shared/ui` genuinely *is* the primitive
  layer and Contentful is already its main consumer.
- **State today on `pdp-token-class-spike` (VERIFIED):** `shared/ui/Button/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx}`
  exist, `components/button/` was deleted, there is **no barrel** at
  `overrides/app/components/shared/ui/index.tsx`, and the only consumer is
  `pages/dev-components/index.tsx` via a relative import. `collectionHero` still imports `Button`
  from the SFCC barrel, so it still renders raw Chakra. It is a relocation with one
  dev-catalogue consumer; the thing it is *for* isn't happening yet.
- Two housekeeping items ride along: that file's docstring still claims it *"Overrides
  `.../shared/ui/Button` via the PWA Kit ccExtensibility resolver"*, which per T1 it does not —
  it will mislead the next reader. And `generateRegistry.mjs` currently **excludes** `/shared/ui`
  from base scanning, which is why the family is invisible in the registry; extending it needs the
  A-or-B answer first so it reports the right thing.

### O3. Storybook vs the in-app dev catalogues — no canonical gallery declared

- **VERIFIED.** `overrides/app/pages/dev-components/index.tsx` exists on
  `feature/pdp-token-class-spike` and `f2r-component-registry`; `dev-design/index.tsx` on
  `f2r-component-registry` only. Neither is on `develop` or on this branch. Reported sizes at the
  time: ~307 and ~1103 lines. Correctly gated —
  `...(process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' ? [ /* dev routes */ ] : [])` — so tree-shaken in
  production with no exposure risk.
- **The unresolved part.** `components.md` mandates a Storybook story for every exported
  component and calls Storybook "the canonical place to view components in isolation". The dev
  pages are a *second* gallery surface, ~1,400 lines. **Nobody has said which is canonical**, and
  the risk named in-session is maintaining both badly.
- **Argument for Storybook as canonical:** already mandated, already has `play`-function coverage
  wired into CI, and is where the six ui-kit components' 55 stories live today.
- **Argument for the in-app catalogue:** it renders inside the real app with the real theme,
  fonts and resolver — so it is immune to T3, which Storybook is not. Combined with per-branch
  preview URLs it lets a designer review without a local checkout.
- A middle position implied but never ratified: Storybook canonical for component API/states,
  in-app catalogue for token/theme review (`/dev/design`) where real-resolver fidelity matters.

`generateRegistry.mjs` on the spike branch gained a `BASE_COMPONENT_ALLOWLIST` — ~60 base

## Quick reference — what a developer does today

1. **New Zimmermann design-system component?**
   `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/<atoms|molecules|organisms>/<camelCase>/index.tsx`
   \+ `index.stories.tsx`. Tier by A3 (what your own template renders — icons-as-props and
   slotted children don't count).
2. **Overriding an SFCC component?** Kebab-case mirror path at
   `overrides/app/components/<kebab-name>/`, exactly matching upstream. Copy-first per AGENTS.md.
   **On `develop` only 7 directories exist under `overrides/app/components/`** (VERIFIED:
   `_app-config`, `button`, `contentful`, `foundation`, `header`, `icons`, `pageContainer`) — so
   most stories still pay the copy-first cost. This branch adds `footer/` and `ui-kits/` for 9.
3. **Styling?** Theme recipe in `theme/components/<camelCase>.ts`, registered under a PascalCase
   (and `Zimm`-namespaced, if it collides) key in `theme/components/index.ts`. Read it with
   `useStyleConfig` (single-part) or `useMultiStyleConfig` (multi-part). `chakra.<el>` +
   `__css={styles.part}` for native elements.
4. **Data?** Presentational named export with required props; thin default-export container for
   fetching/fixtures/navigation. Never a fixture as a prop default.
5. **Before assuming an override propagates?** Grep the base package for who imports that exact
   path (A15). Check for conditional alternates too (T2).
6. **Before trusting the registry?** Its Tier column is a hand-copied duplicate (T9) and its prop
   extraction is regex-based (T6).

## Placement claim — verified, matches exactly

`ls overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` on this branch: `atoms/` = `zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput`; `molecules/` = `zimmInputAction`. `organisms/` **does not exist** (absent, not empty). Git history confirms the reversal order you flagged: `dc86c13` moved `overrides/app/ui-kits/` → `components/ui-kits/`, flattened files to folder-per-component **and dropped the tiers**; `39ad495` restored them as pure `R100` renames. The move under `components/` is what made them registry-visible — `generateRegistry.mjs` only scans `overrides/app/components/`.

Also confirmed: **7** directories under `overrides/app/components/` on `develop` (`_app-config`, `button`, `contentful`, `foundation`, `header`, `icons`, `pageContainer`); this branch adds `footer/` and `ui-kits/` for 9.

## Highest-confidence findings that change how code gets written

**The `shared/ui` barrel trap — re-verified by execution.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` is `export {Button} from './Button'` (relative — the resolver only rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`). Grep counts: **208** base files import the barrel, **0** import `shared/ui/Button`. Upstream `shared/ui/Button/index.jsx` is literally `export {Button} from '@chakra-ui/react'`. The retraction is explicit in-transcript.

**A second, undocumented instance of the same family:** overriding `footer` does **not** reach `/checkout`. Base `_app/index.jsx:484` is `{!isCheckout ? <Footer /> : <CheckoutFooter />}`, and `CheckoutFooter` resolves to `app/pages/checkout/partials/checkout-footer` — a different module your override doesn't shadow. Generalised rule: grep for *conditional renders of alternates*, not just imports of your path.

**`overrideStyling.md` cites 11 paths; 10 are missing on this branch.** Only `theme/components/button.ts` exists. Consequences: the **SFCC bridge pattern has no live example** (its precedent `product-tile`/`CardBaseline` is on another branch), and the pre-PR audit it *mandates* (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`) doesn't exist. Also `grep -rn forwardRef overrides/app/` returns nothing, so the bridge pattern's forwardRef requirement has nothing in-tree to check against.

**The registry reports every design-system atom as Tier 4 Feature-local.** `generateRegistry.mjs:122` hardcodes tier arrays that "mirror" `.claude/rules/` (i.e. duplicate them), no `ui-kits` path is listed, and `getTier()` defaults to `'4 — Feature-local'`. Don't use that column as authority.

**Two registry-generator bugs worth reading as a pair** (`13add6e`, then `ec9d161`): a regex requiring an object-literal body couldn't parse a union alias, so it fell through to merge-everything and published `ZimmButton` as requiring `label` *and* `icon` — a combination the type forbids. The follow-up fix is the instructive one: partial unions were published as complete, and requiredness depended on operand order. Same failure shape recurred in a story-coverage audit, where "0 references in the component's own story file" couldn't distinguish uncovered / covered-by-consumer / dead API — the corrected rule is that a **slot prop's correct test level is the consumer that fills it**.

**Two API patterns worth copying**, both verified in-tree: `ZimmButton`'s discriminated union encodes the a11y contract in the type (`label` required in both members, doubling as `aria-label` for the icon variant — an unlabelled icon button is unconstructible); and `clearable?: boolean` defaulting **off** as the pattern for an affordance absent from the design-system spec.

The genuinely open items I report as open: F2R's kebab folders vs agreed camelCase (O1), the `shared/ui` barrel Option A/B (O2), and Storybook vs the in-app `/dev/*` catalogues — where `components.md` mandates Storybook but the dev pages are immune to the resolver trap that Storybook isn't (O3).
